issues.description: The problem statement requires a method named checkOrderReady() on SealSaloon (used by order processing logic), but the solution implements the same logic in a method named processOrders() and does not provide checkOrderReady(). This name/signature mismatch between the specification and the solution can confuse students about the expected method name and the required API.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method names consistent. Either (A) rename processOrders() in src/de/tum/cit/ase/SealSaloon.java to checkOrderReady(), or (B) add a public checkOrderReady() wrapper that calls the existing processOrders() implementation. Also update the problem statement to reference the same method name if the alternative name (processOrders) is preferred.

issues.description: The problem statement (and UML) requires a method named checkOrderReady() on SealSaloon that is invoked after orderMeal() to attempt serving queued orders. The provided solution implements the same behavior under a different public method name processOrders(). This name divergence (checkOrderReady vs. processOrders) breaks the one-to-one mapping between the exercise specification and the implementation and may confuse students expecting to implement or call checkOrderReady().
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent name for the method that processes/serves pending orders. Either rename the solution method processOrders() to checkOrderReady() (and keep orderMeal() calling it), or update the problem statement/UML to specify processOrders() instead of checkOrderReady(), so students see the same identifier in the specification and implementation.
